commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 85 encoded the solar section 301 / section 201 predicate as hts_number == "8541.42.00.10", one PV-cell line standing for the whole heading 9903.91.02 membership ('articles the product of China, as provided for in subdivision (c) of U.S. note 31 to this subchapter'), and the other four predicates as out-of-chapter exemplars, so every other chapter 85 line the notes list took no section 301 or reciprocal-exclusion treatment.
triage.triage_notes: Same hunk pattern as index 72, with the chapter-specific wrinkle that exemplar line e (8541.42.00.10) IS a chapter 85 line, so the defect here is under-inclusive membership rather than a wholly foreign-chapter condition; the other four exemplars remain out of chapter. Verified the post-fix file references entry_is_line_* 19 times with no local definitions. Same doubt as index 72 about the retained 'runtime semantics are unchanged' boilerplate and the multi-commit repair (follow-up c27e3d99f replaces flags c and e with membership-semantic inputs, which is where chapter 85's solar coverage is properly re-grounded).
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical plumbing and could not: the ch85 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas and proof atoms ground chapter-85 incidence on other chapters' statistical reporting numbers (7202.11.10.00 ferroalloy, 7601.10.30.00 aluminum, 9506.62.40.40 footballs, 2203.00.00.30 beer) plus the single PV line 8541.42.00.10, so the module's output surface shrinks by five rules and the flags become caller inputs — formulas, outputs and scope all change, which excludes "mechanical". Those predicates drove real chapter-85 components (china_section_301_component_rate is a sum of the five exemplar terms; entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded is literally `formula: entry_is_line_a`), so pre-fix the module positively asserted that a chapter-85 entry's §301 and reciprocal-annex incidence turns on equality with non-chapter-85 HTS numbers — four of which can never hold for a chapter-85 line. The companion-test diff confirms the grounding was live, not decorative: the pre-fix ch85 test fed `input.hts_number: 7202.11.10.00` to the chapter-85 module and expected `entry_is_line_a: holds`. That is a condition with no basis in the module's cited chapter-85 source, grounded on the wrong provision, and the fix removes it — untraceable_branch as the first reader classified it, so I confirm rather than reclassify.
triage.verifier_notes:
Refutation attempts and why they failed. (1) "Summary says runtime semantics unchanged" — that sentence ("This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values ... Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged") is generator boilerplate about the parenthesization/scalar-rename serialization and appears verbatim in the PRE file too, so it is no evidence that this change is inert. (2) "Enhancement / new coverage the module never claimed" — the module is a chapter-wide composition (schedule_base_general_rate does ch85_general_rate[hts_line] over the whole chapter table) and it emitted the five flags as outputs, so it made a false chapter-85 claim rather than declining to claim. (3) "Defined elsewhere via import" — checked: no import defines entry_is_line_*; only the untouched hand-built witness composition (us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml) does, and generated chapters do not import it.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh. This commit is one step of the PR #1300 stack: after it, ch85 still carries the exemplar coupling (`section_122_component_rate`: "if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0" at post line 2571, same at brazil/forced-labor §301 3038/3196, and `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` still `formula: entry_is_line_a`). The membership re-grounding the PR body describes ("gated on `entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered`", "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins") landed in later commits, so this commit removes the mis-grounded definitions and defers the correct membership to the caller rather than fixing the incidence inside the module. Kind is a near-tie for entry_is_line_e alone — 8541.42.00.10 is a genuine chapter-85 PV line standing in for the whole 9903.91.02 / note 31(c) membership, which reads as wrong_entity_or_scope — but a through d are grounded on other chapters entirely and the fix shape is removal, which is the untraceable_branch signature, so the kind holds for the change as a whole. I did not run resolve_provision: the defect does not hinge on a number, boundary or clause in the source text, only on the module's own proof atoms citing corpus paths for other chapters' lines, which the diff shows directly.
